canopy.silhouette: huge grey bottle trunk, sparse root-like crown

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling has broad cotyledons and simple, undivided first leaves; hand-shaped leaves with 3, then 5-7 leaflets come later. Young baobabs look nothing like adults: a slender, straight, tapering grey-green whip over a swollen tuberous taproot, with thin branches; the huge bottle trunk and wide crown form only after decades. Seeds are hard and germinate slowly unless scarified.
growth.source: Ethiopian Forestry Dev. baobab study (simple juvenile leaves, 5-7-foliate adult leaves, trees over 1000 yr); Anjarwalla et al. 2021 bioRxiv (seed-grown trees first flower at 8-23 yr; acid-treated seed sprouts in ~5 d); Patrut et al. 2018 Nature Plants (radiocarbon ages to ~2500 yr); height curve estimated

fruiting.source: Venter & Witkowski 2019 For Ecol Manage (southern Africa: flowering 1-5 months peaking Nov, 290-710 flowers per tree, fruit set ~20%); EFD Ethiopia study (57-157 fruits/tree in Benin, 77 in South Africa); Baum 1995 (pendent white flowers open at dusk for one night, fruit-bat pollination)

canopy.name: Umbrella thorn

canopy.silhouette: flat-topped disc on bare thorny limbs

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two oval cotyledons, then tiny feathery bipinnate leaves on a thin stem with paired spines, some long, straight and white, others short and hooked. The taproot dives deep first. Browsed saplings become dense, low, cage-like spiny bushes for years; once a leader escapes browsers it gains about 1.5 m in two years and only later spreads the flat umbrella crown.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (Acacia tortilis): up to 21 m, about 1.5 m in 2 years, a 6-7-year-old tree yields 5-6 kg of clean seed, 10-12 kg pods a year at 10 yr; Andersen & Krzywinski 2007 (BMC Ecology): radiocarbon ages of 200-650 yr for trees in Egypt's Eastern Desert, radial growth up to 2.4 mm a year. Germination and height curve estimated.

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (Acacia tortilis): white or pale yellowish-white heads 0.5-1.1 cm, pods 7-10 cm by 6-10 mm, spirally twisted, 10-12 kg pods per 10-yr tree; the Turkana make porridge from the pods, the Maasai eat immature seeds; Wikipedia: aromatic flowers, springlike coiled pods. Flowering at the onset of the rains, ripening, pod fall and rot times estimated.

canopy.silhouette: small open feathery tree, mottled pale trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two thick rounded cotyledons, then small feathery pinnate leaves of rounded leaflets. It grows as a thin whip that, in the drought-deciduous Caatinga, drops its leaves each dry season and often forks low, becoming a small multi-branched tree with smooth mottled bark.
growth.source: Flora do Brasil / Reflora (Cenostigma pyramidale: Caatinga tree 4-12 m, yellow flowers in terminal racemes, flat woody pods with explosive dehiscence); Brazilian seed-technology studies of catingueira (fast, high germination without dormancy); growth and ages estimated

fruiting.source: Flora do Brasil (yellow flowers in racemes during the rains, flat woody pods that twist open explosively); phenology studies in Caatinga (flowering with the rains Dec-Apr, bee-pollinated); counts and timings estimated from related Caesalpinia/Libidibia

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 leafy cotyledons, then glossy, leathery, narrow lance-shaped leaves. The sapling is a slow, slender whip with dark bark that takes decades to overtop the thorny Chaco scrub; the adult has a straight trunk of extremely hard red heartwood and a rounded, open, semi-evergreen crown.
growth.source: Wikipedia Schinopsis balansae (to 24 m, trunk over 1 m; wood density 1.2, 'axe-breaker'; quebracho tannin); Flora Argentina/Anacardiaceae (dioecious, small panicled flowers, one-winged samara); Chaco quebracho growth studies (very slow diameter growth); germination, growth curve and ages estimated

fruiting.source: Flora Argentina and Chaco forestry notes on quebracho colorado (dioecious; tiny whitish-green flowers in terminal panicles in the southern summer; one-winged samara ripening reddish-brown in autumn, wind-dispersed); insect pollination as in other Anacardiaceae; counts and timing estimated

shrub.silhouette: sparse twiggy shrub with peeling papery bark

growth.juvenile_note: Seed germination is slow and poor, so most new plants start as fallen branches or stakes that root. The seedling is a small spiny stem with trifoliate leaves; young roots are swollen, juicy and water-storing. It grows slowly into a squat, spiny, much-branched small tree with peeling grey-green papery bark that bleeds aromatic resin when cut.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Commiphora africana (small tree usually <5 m, rarely 10 m; flowers in the first half of the dry season before the leaves; 4 red petals forming a ~6 mm tube; reddish resinous fruits 6-8 mm; juicy sweet roots of young plants chewed); germination, growth and ages estimated from Commiphora literature

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Commiphora africana (red 4-petalled flowers ~6 mm on leafless spur shoots early in the dry season; fruits reddish, resinous, 6-8 mm, splitting to show a hard stone dispersed by birds and animals); ripening and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Mostly spread by broken stems (cuttings root in 2-4 weeks); seedlings are rare. The young plant is a few pencil-thin, smooth, bright green succulent sticks with tiny linear leaves at the tips that soon fall, forking repeatedly into a bushy tangle of green twigs; lower stems turn grey-brown and woody with age.
growth.source: Estimated from Useful Tropical Plants and PROTA accounts of Euphorbia tirucalli (fast-growing succulent shrub or tree to 7-10 m, hedge plant grown from cuttings, dioecious, seed rarely set in cultivation).

traits.leaf_shape: stiff spined sword leaves in a rosette
traits.trunk: none or a short woody stem; tall flower spike
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are rarely seen; nearly all young rosettes are pups rising from rhizomes about 10 cm down, spreading 2-3 times the parent's width, so plants form dense colonies. A young rosette is a tight upright cup of a few stiff, thick, yellow-green, slightly incurved leaves with small down-hooked edge teeth and a sharp tip spine; it adds only 4-11 leaves a year.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Agave lechuguilla: 50% germination in ~4 days at 25-30 C; 3.9-10.8 new leaves/plant/yr; rosette of 20-50 leaves, 20-60 cm; leaves live 12-15 yr; flowers once, typically at 10-20 yr (stalk 1-4 m), then dies and is replaced by clones; rhizomes ~10 cm deep; seedlings rarely observed. Rosette size-age estimated.

epiphyte.silhouette: small grey ball tufts on branches

growth.juvenile_note: Plumed seeds stick to twigs, bark and even power lines; the seedling is a tiny grey tuft of thin, curved, scaly leaves. Shoots branch as they grow, so within a few years a young plant becomes a spiky grey tuft and then a round ball of many recurved shoots, golf-ball to soccer-ball size, each sending up a thin stalk with one or two small pale-violet flowers.
growth.source: Wikipedia Tillandsia recurvata (ball moss: balls golf-ball to soccer-ball size made of many joined shoots; seeds plentiful, with fine hairs; southern USA to Argentina and Chile; favours humid, sheltered sites; frost-sensitive). Flowering age, growth and ball lifespan estimated.
